etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English you, yow, ȝow (object case of ye), from Old English ēow (“you”, dative case of ġē), from Proto-Germanic *iwwiz (“you”, dative case of *jīz), Western form of *izwiz (“you”, dative case of *jūz), from Proto-Indo-European *yūs (“you”, plural), *yū́.

Cognate with Scots you (“you”), Saterland Frisian jou (“you”), West Frisian jo (“you”), Low German jo, joe and oe (“you”), Dutch jou and u (“you”), Middle High German eu, iu (“you”, object pronoun), Latin vōs (“you”), Avestan 𐬬𐬋 (vō, “you”), Ashkun yë̃́ (“you”), Kamkata-viri šó (“you”), Sanskrit यूयम् (yūyám, “you”)

See usage notes. Ye, you and your are cognate with Dutch jij/je, jou, jouw; Low German ji, jo/ju, jug and German ihr, euch and euer respectively. Ye is also cognate with Danish I and archaic Swedish I.

definitions.definition: (object pronoun) The people spoken, or written to, as an object. [from 9th c.]

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Genesis 42:14, column 1:
quote.text: And Ioſeph ſaid vnto them, That is it that I ſpake vnto you, ſaying, Ye are ſpies.

definitions.definition: (reflexive pronoun, now US colloquial) (To) yourselves, (to) yourself. [from 9th c.]

quote.citation: c. 1593 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedy of Richard the Third: […]”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, (please specify the act number in uppercase Roman numerals, and the scene number in lowercase Roman numerals):
quote.text: If I may counsaile you, some day or two / Your Highnesse shall repose you at the Tower [...].

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Genesis XIX::
quote.text: And Lot went out, and spake unto his sons in law, which married his daughters, and said, Up, get you out of this place; for the Lord will destroy this city.

quote.citation: 1886 October – 1887 January, H[enry] Rider Haggard, She: A History of Adventure, London: Longmans, Green, and Co., published 1887, →OCLC:
quote.text: 'Draw near, and wash you in the living flames, and take their virtue into your poor frames in all its virgin strength[.]'

quote.citation: 1970, Donald Harington, Lightning Bug:
quote.text: ‘Pull you up a chair,’ she offered.

quote.citation: 1975, Joseph Nazel, Death for Hire:
quote.text: You'd better get you a gun and kill him before he kills you or somebody.

definitions.definition: (object pronoun) The person spoken to or written to, as an object. (Replacing thee; originally as a mark of respect.) [from 13th c.]

quote.citation: c. 1485, Thomas Malory, Le Morte Darthur, Book VIII:
quote.text: I charge you, as ye woll have my love, that ye warne your kynnesmen that ye woll beare that day the slyve of golde uppon your helmet.

definitions.definition: (subject pronoun) The people spoken to or written to, as a subject. (Replacing ye.) [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 2016, VOA Learning English (public domain)
quote.text:
Are you excited?  ―  Yes, I am excited!
Audio (US):(file)

definitions.definition: (subject pronoun) The person spoken to or written to, as a subject. (Originally as a mark of respect.) [from 15th c.]

quote.citation: 1814 May 9, [Jane Austen], chapter IX, in Mansfield Park: […], volume II, London:  […]  [George Sidney] for T[homas] Egerton, […], →OCLC, page 208:
quote.text: You are right, Fanny, to protest against such an office, but you need not be afraid.

definitions.definition: (object pronoun, colloquial) A person's favorite sports team.
(indefinite personal pronoun) Anyone, one; an unspecified individual or group of individuals (as subject or object). [from 16th c.]

quote.citation: 2001 May 5, Polly Vernon, The Guardian:
quote.text: You can't choose your family, your lovers are difficult and volatile, but, oh, you can choose your friends - so doesn't it make much more sense to live and holiday with them instead?

definitions.definition: (indefinite personal pronoun) A dummy pronoun used in certain constructions, usually with verbs of receiving (such as get or find) or sensing (such as see or hear), typically stating the existence or typicality of something.

quote.citation: 1973, Soldiers:
quote.text: You find a lot of 'life' in the city but much of it is an act people are putting on.

quote.citation: 2018 October 4, Javier Marías, Berta Isla, Penguin UK, →ISBN:
quote.text: You get some terrible bullies in Spanish villages too , and they'll doubtless grow up to be complete oafs.

quote.citation: 2018 January 16, Rick Wolff, Secrets of Sports Psychology Revealed: Proven Techniques to Elevate Your Performance, Simon and Schuster, →ISBN:
quote.text: You often hear about athletes having the jitters before a game, or having butterflies in their stomach.

definitions.definition: The individual or group spoken or written to.
Used before epithets, describing the person being addressed, for emphasis.

quote.citation: 2015, Judi Curtin, Only Eva, The O'Brien Press, →ISBN:
quote.text: 'You genius!' I shouted in Aretta's ear. 'You absolute genius! Why didn't you tell us you were so good?'

definitions.definition: (transitive) To address (a person) using the pronoun you (in the past, especially to use you rather than thou, when you was considered more formal).

quote.citation: 1930, Barrington Hall, Modern Conversation, Brewer & Warren, page 239:
quote.text: Youing consists in relating everything in the conversation to the person you wish to flatter, and introducing the word “you” into your speech as often as possible.

quote.citation: 1992, Barbara Anderson, Portrait of the Artist’s Wife, Victoria University Press, page 272:
quote.text: Now even Princess Anne had dropped it. Sarah had heard her youing away on television the other night just like the inhabitants of her mother’s dominions beyond the seas.

quote.citation: 2004, Ellen Miller, “Practicing”, in Brooklyn Noir, Akashic Books:
quote.text: But even having my very own personal pronoun was risky, because it’s pretty tough to keep stopped-hope stopped up when you are getting all youed up, when someone you really like keeps promising you scary, fun, exciting stuff—and even tougher for the of that moment to remain securely devoid of hope, to make smart, self-denying decisions with Dad youing me—the long ooo of it broad and extended, like a hand.

definitions.definition: The name of the Latin-script letter U/u.

quote.citation: 1969, Michael Feld, The Sabbatical Year, London: Alan Ross Ltd, page 301:
quote.text: ‘Eff. You. En,’ said Mr Banstead. ‘Fun! […]’

quote.citation: 2004, Will Rogers, The Stonking Steps, page 170:
quote.text: It said, in a whispering, buzzing voice, "Gee-you-ess-ess-ay-dash-em-ee-ar-ar-wye-dash-em-eye-en-gee-oh-dash-pee-eye-pee-dash-pee-ee-ar-ar-wye-dash-pee-eye-en-gee-oh."

quote.citation: 2019, Anand Ranganathan, Chitra Subramaniam, The Rat Eater, Bloomsbury India, →ISBN:
quote.text: ‘S-S-C…sitting on a tree…eff-you-cee-kay-i-en-ji.’
